title: A principal localization of a one-dimensional local domain is its fraction field
statement: Let B be a local integral domain of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], let K=Frac(B) be its fraction field, and let 0\ne f belong to the maximal ideal of B. Let B_f denote the localization away from f [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Then the localization map B_f\to K is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemmas Tags 00CM and 00C8 (localization and the prime correspondence for a localization)

proof.text: Apply Mathlib ringKrullDim_eq_one_iff_of_isLocalRing_isDomain to obtain, for each nonzero b in B, that the maximal ideal is contained in the radical of (b). Since f belongs to the maximal ideal, Ideal.mem_radical_iff and Ideal.mem_span_singleton give a natural number n with b dividing f^n. Every power of f is a non-zero-divisor because B is a domain and f is nonzero.

The divisibility just established and IsLocalization.of_le_of_exists_dvd show that the explicit ring Localization.Away f is also the localization at the non-zero-divisors of B. Both it and K are therefore fraction rings of B. The given Away.lift commutes with the maps from B by IsLocalization.Away.lift_comp, so IsLocalization.bijective at the non-zero-divisors proves it bijective. No field structure or arbitrary witness is chosen.

proof_origin.note: Direct Mathlib proof using the radical characterization of dimension one and uniqueness of localization; replaces the prime-spectrum argument below the unit level.
